title: Find Nth Smallest Integer With K One Bits
summary: Given positive integers n and k, find the n-th smallest positive integer with exactly k ones in its binary representation, ensuring the result is less than 2^50.
statement: Given positive integers n and k, find the n-th smallest positive integer with exactly k ones in its binary representation, ensuring the result is less than 2^50.
constraints: n and k are positive and the guaranteed answer is below 2^50.
Return the nth integer whose binary representation contains exactly k one bits.
hints: Among values using positions 0..p, exactly C(p,k) have bit p equal to zero and k ones below it.
Construct the answer from bit 49 downward, comparing n with the size of the zero-bit group.
If n exceeds that group, subtract it, set the bit, and reduce the remaining one count.
This is lexicographic unranking of fixed-size bit-position subsets, which matches numeric order from the highest bit downward.
editorial: This is lexicographic unranking of fixed-size bit-position subsets, which matches numeric order from the highest bit downward.

tests.explanation: The sequence begins 3,5,6,9, so the fourth value is nine.
The one-bit values are 1,2,4,…, making the third value four.
